findings.headline: Top risk-adjusted outlier (z_adj 26.5). 99215 on 27% of claims vs 1.7% expected. Random sample of 30 charts: 7 below billed level; 4 of 8 documented 99215s were below the billed level (peers 9%).
findings.interpretation: The high share is mostly on healthy patients: 24% of visits with 0 chronic conditions were billed 99215 (peers 2.2%), and 84% of its 99215s were on patients with 0–1 conditions. The charts back up the claims pattern. Draft overpayment estimate from the complete random sample: $11,492 (CI $5,486–$17,497). A certified coder should review this before any recovery.

findings.headline: z_adj 12.5. 99215 on 19% of claims vs 2.1% expected. 6 of 19 returned charts were below billed; 6 of 13 documented 99214/99215s were below the billed level (peers 6%).
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is high at every complexity level, including 12% on patients with 0 conditions (peers 2.2%). Caveat: only 19 of 30 random-sample charts came back. The office left out 11 visits and then objected, so the sample may not be random any more. Treat the $10,247 estimate (CI $3,790–$16,704) with caution until the missing charts are obtained or a coder confirms it.

findings.headline: z_adj 11.4, but the panel is much sicker than average (238 visits with 5+ conditions). Charts support billing: 2 of 30 below billed.
findings.interpretation: Its 99215s are concentrated on patients with many conditions. Share on 0-condition patients is 6.4%, the lowest of those reviewed. The random-sample charts mostly support the billed levels. Share is still above peers within each complexity level, so periodic monitoring is reasonable. No recovery referral.

findings.headline: z_adj 14.4. 99215 on 21% of claims. Charts mostly support billing: 2 of 30 below billed.
findings.interpretation: Sick panel (73% 99215 on patients with 5+ conditions), but the share on 0-condition patients (8.9% vs 2.2%) is also high. Charts did not confirm upcoding. Not enough to call either way.

findings.headline: z_adj 11.0. 99215 on 24% of claims, 15% on 0-condition patients. Charts: 0 of 30 below billed.
findings.interpretation: The documentation supports the billed levels, but the claims pattern on healthy patients is still well above peers. Only 3 of 30 notes described data review with no matching test on the claim, so there is little sign of notes padded to fit the bill. Inconclusive.

findings.headline: z_adj 13.1. 99215 on 37% of claims, 26% on 0-condition patients. Charts: 2 of 30 below billed.
findings.interpretation: The claims pattern on healthy patients is striking, but the random-sample charts largely support the billed levels. That gap could mean the documentation is real or that notes are written to match the bill. The tools gave no evidence for either, so this stays inconclusive. A coder could look for copied-forward notes.

findings.headline: z_adj 16.0 on a high volume (2,377 claims). Charts: 1 of 30 below billed (after a wrong-dates resubmission).
findings.interpretation: Moderately high on 0-condition patients (7.6% vs 2.2%), but the charts support billing. No chart evidence of upcoding.
